rows.stem: Tooth enamel is made up of calcium hydroxyapatite (a crystalline form of calcium phosphate). This chemical starts corroding in the mouth when the pH is :
rows.solution:
Bacteria in the mouth break down sugar and food particles left after eating and produce acids, which lower the pH. Tooth enamel, calcium hydroxyapatite, starts to corrode when the pH in the mouth falls below \(5{\cdot}5\).

Of the values given, only pH 5 is below \(5{\cdot}5\), which is option (B) 5.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The phenomenon responsible for making the smoke particles visible when a beam of sunlight enters a smoke filled room through a narrow hole is :
rows.solution:
The beam of sunlight becomes visible because the tiny smoke particles in its path scatter the light towards our eyes. This is the Tyndall effect, caused by the scattering of light by colloidal particles.

This is option (A) scattering of light.

rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Use mirror formula to determine the position of the image formed by this mirror.
rows.solution:
For a concave mirror the focal length is negative, \(f = -15\) cm, and the object is in front of the mirror, \(u = -10\) cm.

Mirror formula: \(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{-2 + 3}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}\).

So \(v = +30\) cm. The image is formed 30 cm from the mirror, behind it. The object lies between the pole and the focus, so the image is virtual, erect and magnified.

rows.stem: Consider two lamps A and B of rating 50 W; 220 V and 25 W; 220 V respectively. Find the ratio of the resistances of the two lamps (i.e. \(\mathrm{R_A} : \mathrm{R_B}\)).
rows.solution:
For a lamp of power P rated at voltage V, \(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\), so \(R = \dfrac{V^2}{P}\).

\(R_A = \dfrac{(220)^2}{50} = 968\,\Omega\) and \(R_B = \dfrac{(220)^2}{25} = 1936\,\Omega\).

\(\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{(220)^2/50}{(220)^2/25} = \dfrac{25}{50} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

So \(R_A : R_B = 1 : 2\). Both lamps are rated at the same voltage, so the resistance is inversely proportional to the power: lamp A has twice the power, and so half the resistance.

rows.stem: Heat produced per second due to a current in a resistor of \(4\,\Omega\) is 400 joules. Calculate the potential difference across the resistor.
rows.solution:
The heat produced in a resistor is \(H = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\,t\).

Here \(H = 400\) J, \(t = 1\) s and \(R = 4\,\Omega\), so \(400 = \dfrac{V^2}{4} \times 1\).

\(V^2 = 1600\), so \(V = 40\) V.

The potential difference across the resistor is 40 V.

rows.stem:
Translate the following statements into chemical equations and then balance them :

(a) Nitric acid reacts with calcium hydroxide to form calcium nitrate and water.

(b) Sodium chloride reacts with silver nitrate to form silver chloride and sodium nitrate.
rows.solution:
(a) Nitric acid and calcium hydroxide give calcium nitrate and water:

\(\mathrm{2HNO_3 + Ca(OH)_2 \rightarrow Ca(NO_3)_2 + 2H_2O}\)

(b) Sodium chloride and silver nitrate give a white precipitate of silver chloride and sodium nitrate:

\(\mathrm{NaCl + AgNO_3 \rightarrow AgCl + NaNO_3}\)

Each equation must be balanced: the marking scheme deducts half a mark for an unbalanced one.

rows.stem:
(a) Define one volt potential difference between two points in an electric field.

(b) Draw a schematic diagram of an electric circuit of a cell of \(1{\cdot}5\) V, \(5\,\Omega\) and \(10\,\Omega\) resistor and a plug key, all connected in series. Calculate the current drawn from the cell when the key is closed.
rows.solution:
(a) The potential difference between two points is one volt when one joule of work is done to move a charge of one coulomb from one point to the other: \(1\,\mathrm{V} = \dfrac{1\,\mathrm{J}}{1\,\mathrm{C}}\).

(b) The circuit diagram: draw the cell (\(1{\cdot}5\) V), the \(5\,\Omega\) resistor, the \(10\,\Omega\) resistor and the plug key one after another in a single closed loop, so that all four are in series, with arrows showing the direction of the current.

The resistors are in series, so the total resistance is \(R = 5 + 10 = 15\,\Omega\).

\(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{1{\cdot}5}{15} = 0{\cdot}1\) A.

The current drawn from the cell is \(0{\cdot}1\) A.

rows.stem:
(a) How many chromosomes are present in human beings ? Out of these how many are sex chromosomes ?

(b) Explain how, in sexually reproducing organisms, the number of chromosomes in the progeny is maintained.
rows.solution:
(a) Human beings have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in each body cell. Of these, 2 chromosomes (one pair) are sex chromosomes.

(b) In sexually reproducing organisms the chromosomes in body cells occur in pairs. When the germ cells (gametes) form, the members of each pair separate, so each gamete carries only half the number of chromosomes, one from each pair.

At fertilisation a male gamete and a female gamete fuse to form the zygote, which gets one set of chromosomes from each parent. This restores the original number of chromosomes, so the progeny has the same number as its parents.

rows.stem:
A hormone ‘X’ is secreted in blood when a person is under scary situation.

(a) Identify the hormone ‘X’ and the gland that secretes it.

(b) Explain its role in dealing with scary or emergency situations.
rows.solution:
(a) The hormone X is adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands.

(b) Adrenaline is secreted directly into the blood and carried to different parts of the body, preparing it to deal with the emergency:

1. It acts on the heart, which beats faster, resulting in a greater supply of oxygen to the skeletal muscles.

2. The blood supply to the digestive system and the skin is reduced, because the muscles around the small arteries in these organs contract. This diverts blood to the skeletal muscles.

3. The breathing rate increases because of contractions of the diaphragm and the rib muscles.

Together these responses prepare the body to fight or to run away.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw electron dot structure of chlorine molecule.

(Atomic Number of Chlorine = 17)

(ii) What happens when chlorine reacts with methane in the presence of sunlight ? Write the name of the reaction.

(iii) Name the two oxidising agents used for the conversion of alcohols to acids.

(iv) List four differences in properties between covalent compounds and ionic compounds.
rows.solution:
(i) Chlorine (atomic number 17) has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 7, so each atom has seven valence electrons and needs one more to complete its octet.

In the electron dot structure of \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\), each chlorine atom contributes one electron to a shared pair between the two atoms (a single covalent bond, Cl-Cl). Each atom also keeps three lone pairs, so each has eight electrons around it.

(ii) In the presence of sunlight, chlorine replaces the hydrogen atoms of methane one by one. In the first step chloromethane is formed:

\(\mathrm{CH_4 + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} CH_3Cl + HCl}\)

This is a substitution reaction.

(iii) Any two: alkaline potassium permanganate (\(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\)), acidified potassium permanganate, acidified potassium dichromate (\(\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}\)).

(iv) Four differences:

1. Covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points; ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.

2. Covalent compounds are generally poor conductors of electricity; ionic compounds conduct electricity in aqueous solution and in the molten state.

3. Covalent compounds that are solids are generally soft; ionic compounds are hard crystalline solids.

4. Covalent compounds are generally soluble in oil or non-polar solvents; ionic compounds are generally soluble in water and polar solvents.

rows.stem:
(i) Give reason why carbon forms compounds mainly by covalent bonding.

(ii) Why do covalent compounds have low melting and boiling points.

(iii) Give reason for the following :

I. Covalent compounds are bad conductors of electricity.

II. Carbon shows catenation.
rows.solution:
(i) Carbon has four valence electrons (2, 4), and it cannot easily reach a noble gas configuration by forming ions.

It could gain four electrons to form the \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) anion, but it would be difficult for a nucleus with six protons to hold on to ten electrons.

It could lose four electrons to form the \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) cation, but that would need a large amount of energy, leaving a carbon cation with six protons holding only two electrons.

So carbon shares its four valence electrons with other atoms, forming covalent bonds.

(ii) The forces of attraction between the molecules of a covalent compound are weak, so little energy is needed to separate them. Their melting and boiling points are therefore low.

(iii) I. Covalent compounds do not form ions, because their electrons are shared between atoms. With no charged particles to carry the current, they are bad conductors of electricity.

II. Carbon can form bonds with other carbon atoms, giving long chains, branched chains and rings. It shows catenation because the carbon-carbon bond is very strong and stable, owing to the small size of the carbon atom.
